definitions.gloss: Japanese style; in the Japanese manner
definitions.explanation: Having characteristics typical of Japanese aesthetics, design, or customs. Used as a noun or as a modifier with の to describe things done in a Japanese way.

examples.japanese: {日本風|にほんふう}の{庭|にわ}が{好|す}きだ。
この{建物|たてもの}は{日本風|にほんふう}に{建|た}てられている。
examples.english: This building was constructed in the Japanese style.

examples.japanese: {海外|かいがい}のレストランで{日本風|にほんふう}のカレーが{人気|にんき}を{集|あつ}めている。
examples.english: Japanese-style curry is gaining popularity at overseas restaurants.

notes:
Composed of {日本|にほん} (Japan) + {風|ふう} (style, manner). The suffix {風|ふう} is highly productive and attaches to country names, proper nouns, and other words to mean 'in the style of.' Can be used as a noun or as a modifier with の.

COMMON COLLOCATIONS:
- {日本風|にほんふう}の{家|いえ}: Japanese-style house
- {日本風|にほんふう}の{料理|りょうり}: Japanese-style cooking
- {日本風|にほんふう}にアレンジする: to arrange in the Japanese style

SIMILAR PATTERNS WITH {風|ふう}:
- {西洋風|せいようふう}: Western style
- {中華風|ちゅうかふう}: Chinese style
- {洋風|ようふう}: Western/European style
- {和風|わふう}: Japanese style (more common synonym using the {和|わ} prefix)

SIMILAR WORDS:
- {和風|わふう}: Japanese style -- more commonly used in everyday contexts, especially for food and design
- {日本式|にほんしき}: Japanese method/system -- emphasizes the system or method rather than aesthetic style
- {和様|わよう}: Japanese style -- literary/formal, used for architecture and calligraphy
